decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/2 to 3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Measures of consumer and business sentiment have improved of late.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this new note to highlight that people and companies are feeling more confident about the economy.

changes.quote: Inflation increased in recent quarters but is still below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective.
changes.explanation: This simplifies how the Fed describes recent price pressures, removing old details about past declines in energy and import prices.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; most survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.
changes.explanation: The Fed streamlined its assessment of inflation expectations by removing references to recent months.

changes.quote: The Committee expects that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace, labor market conditions will strengthen somewhat further, and inflation will rise to 2 percent over the medium term.
changes.explanation: The Fed explicitly added its expectation that inflation will return to 2 percent over the medium term.

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: This updates the main action from a rate hike in the previous meeting to holding rates steady.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee expects that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace, labor market conditions will strengthen somewhat further, and inflation will rise to 2 percent over the medium term.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a return to 2 percent inflation.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.51% APR costs about $52.12 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.48% and moved +3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.09% would rise by about $5.22 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.7%, and employers added an average of 147k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.1% over the past year (December 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.03%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.14% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate increases will be gradual and depend on incoming economic data.
